unmapped_findings: For the increasing-temperature sample (950→1050 °C, 0.01 s^-1, ε_I=0.4): the experimental average grain size (AGS) drops to a minimum near 0.5 strain and then increases again toward 0.9 strain, i.e. refinement followed by coarsening (Fig. 16d; b0219, figure_016).

3D CA simulation for the increasing-temperature 950→1050 °C condition (0.4–0.5 strain) predicts AGS 65.61 µm at 0.5 strain (99.5% DRX) and 75.90 µm at 0.9 strain (99.8% DRX); experimentally, AGS decreased slightly from 65.33 µm at 0.4 strain (950 °C, 0.01 s^-1) to 62.63 µm at 0.5 strain (Fig. 21; table_005, b0229).

For this sample, after transiently decreasing Z_P (temperature increase), Table 7 gives: AGS of DRXGs_I = 61.89 µm (volume fraction 0.13), AGS of DRXGs_II = 77.83 µm (volume fraction 0.86), and final microstructure AGS = 75.90 µm at 0.9 strain (table_007, b0251).

Flow-stress simulation: the 3D CA reproduces the experimental transient stress drop for the 950→1050 °C (0.4 strain) path, dropping abruptly at ≈0.4 strain toward a low plateau (Fig. 13d; figure_013, b0200).

For the increasing-temperature condition (950→1050 °C, 0.01 s^-1), the DRX fraction rises from 0.757 (0.4 strain) to 0.979 (0.5 strain) experimentally, indicating recrystallization refinement during the temperature rise (b0229, figure_018).
